I have everything I need. Here is the analysis.

---

# FA3 Hopper forward (bf16, hd128, causal, PAGED, persistent) — findings

All paths below are for the config `tile_size_fwd_sm90(128,128,is_causal=true,...)` → `{kBlockM=128, kBlockN=128, MmaPV_is_RS=true, IntraWGOverlap=true}` (`tile_size.h:44`), `kStages=2` (`flash_fwd_launch_template.h:48`), `MmaQK_is_RS=false` (`mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp:84`).

## 1. Q is SINGLE-buffered (1 smem buffer)

K and V carry an explicit `Int<kStages>` stage dimension; **Q does not**. Q's layout is just the (M, headdim) tile with no stage axis:

`mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp:132`
```cpp
using SmemLayoutQ = decltype(tile_to_shape(SmemLayoutAtomQ{}, select<0, 2>(TileShape_MNK{})));
```
vs. K/V which get `Int<kStages>{}` (`:138`, `:144`).

The allocation in `TensorStorage` is a single un-staged array (`TensorStorageWithoutPNoTranspose`, the variant selected because `MmaPV_is_RS=true`), `mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp:319-324`:
```cpp
struct TensorStorageWithoutPNoTranspose : cute::aligned_struct<...> {
    cute::array_aligned<Element, cute::cosize_v<SmemLayoutVt>, SmemAlignmentVtNoTranspose> smem_v;
    cute::array_aligned<Element, cute::cosize_v<SmemLayoutQ>, SmemAlignmentQ> smem_q;   // <-- ONE Q buffer
    cute::array_aligned<Element, cute::cosize_v<SmemLayoutK>, SmemAlignmentK> smem_k;
    SmemQv_t smem_qv;
    cute::array_aligned<ElementSAux, cute::cosize_v<SmemLayoutSAux>, 128> smem_s_aux;
};
```
Correspondingly there is a single (non-pipelined) `barrier_Q` — a lone `BarrierQ`, not a staged pipeline like K/V — `flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h:110`:
```cpp
alignas(16) BarrierQ barrier_Q;
```
So: **1 Q smem buffer, single-buffered.** (K and V each get `kStages=2` buffers.)

## 2. Q (re)loaded via TMA (one async box); the work-tile boundary SERIALIZES on Q

Q is loaded with a single TMA `copy` into `barrier_Q` (not cp.async gather; cp.async is only the `PackGQA` fallback branch). `mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp:850-859`:
```cpp
if constexpr (Use_TMA_Q) {
    // Wait for the MMA warpgroups to signal that smem_q is ready
    if (SingleProducerWarp || warp_idx_in_warpgroup == 0) {
        cutlass::arch::NamedBarrier::sync(NumMmaThreadsQK + cutlass::NumThreadsPerWarp,
            static_cast<uint32_t>(FwdNamedBarriers::QueryEmpty) /*id*/);
    }
    if ((SingleProducerWarp || warp_idx_in_warpgroup == 0) && cute::elect_one_sync()) {
        shared_storage.pipelines.barrier_Q.arrive_and_expect_tx(TmaTransactionBytesQ);
        copy(params.tma_load_Q.with(... barrier_Q ..., 0 /*mcast_mask*/, ...EVICT_FIRST...),
            tQgQ, tQsQ);
```

The gate is the `QueryEmpty` named barrier. Because `MmaQK_is_RS=false`, Q stays resident in smem and is read (SS-GMMA, `tSrQ = wg_mma_qk.partition_fragment_A(sQ)`, `:1067`) on **every** K-block QK GEMM. The consumer therefore only releases Q **after the entire K loop finishes**, at `mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp:1324-1325`:
```cpp
// Tell producers that smem_q is ready
cutlass::arch::NamedBarrier::arrive(NumMmaThreadsQK + (Use_TMA_Q ? cutlass::NumThreadsPerWarp : NumProducerThreads),
    static_cast<uint32_t>(FwdNamedBarriers::QueryEmpty) /*id*/);
```
and the consumer waits on Q at the *top* of the mainloop (`:1168-1170`):
```cpp
auto &barrier_Q = shared_storage.pipelines.barrier_Q;
if constexpr (!AppendKV) {
    barrier_Q.wait(work_idx % 2);
}
```

Sequence per work tile: producer must pass `QueryEmpty` (`:853`) **before** it may re-issue the Q TMA (`:857`); that `QueryEmpty` is only signalled by the consumer at `:1325`, i.e. after the current tile has consumed Q across all its K-blocks. With only one Q buffer, **the next tile's Q reload cannot begin until the current tile's mainloop has fully finished with Q — the boundary serializes on Q; it is not overlapped/prefetched.** (Contrast: the producer freely runs K/V ahead via the 2-stage K/V pipelines and even prefetches the *next work descriptor* at `:921` `scheduler_prefetch()`, but Q itself is not double-buffered so its reload is not hoisted under the current compute.)

## 3. Exact dynamic smem budget (hd128 paged, bf16)

Element = 2 B; kBlockM=kBlockN=kHeadDim=kHeadDimV=128; kStages=2; `MmaPV_is_RS=true` ⇒ `SmemP_t = cute::array<Element,0>` (0 B, no P smem, `:313`); bf16 ⇒ `Transpose_V=false` ⇒ no `smem_vt`; `LargeHeadDimV=false` ⇒ `SmemScale_t`=0 B (`:314`).

Tensor storage (`TensorStorageWithoutPNoTranspose`, `:319-324`):
| buffer | layout | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| `smem_q` | 128×128 | 128·128·2 = **32,768** |
| `smem_k` | 128×128×**2 stages** | 128·128·2·2 = **65,536** |
| `smem_v` | 128×128×**2 stages** | 128·128·2·2 = **65,536** |
| `smem_qv` | HasQv=false | 0 |
| `smem_s_aux` | 64 × bf16 (`ElementS=bfloat16_t`, `flash_fwd_launch_template.h:38`) | 64·2 = **128** |
| P smem | MmaPV_is_RS ⇒ elided | 0 |

Tensor subtotal = 32,768 + 65,536 + 65,536 + 128 = **163,968 B (160.125 KiB)**.

mbarriers / `PipelineStorage` (`flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h:109-119`), each mbarrier 8 B but `alignas(16)`; each pipeline SharedStorage = full[2]+empty[2] = 4·8 = 32 B; scheduler `SharedStorage = int` for the causal `DynamicPersistentTileScheduler` (`tile_scheduler.hpp:239`):
- barrier_Q 16 + barrier_Qv 16 + barrier_O 16 = 48
- pipeline_k 32 + pipeline_v 32 + pipeline_vt 32 + pipeline_k_new 32 + pipeline_v_new 32 = 160
- smem_scheduler (int, padded) ≈ 16
- ≈ **224 B**

Total `SharedStorageSize` ≈ 163,968 + 224 ≈ **164,192 B**, rounded up to the 128-B struct alignment ≈ **164,224 B ≈ 160.4 KiB**.

Against Hopper opt-in max:
- vs **228 KiB** (233,472 B): **~70.3 % used, ~69,248 B ≈ 67.6 KiB headroom**.
- vs the 227 KiB actually settable via `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` (232,448 B): ~66.6 KiB headroom.

(Note the epilogue `smem_o` = 128·128·2 = 32,768 B is **unioned onto `smem_v`**, `flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h:96-107`, so it adds nothing; `mainloop_smem_padding = max(0, sizeof(epilogue)−sizeof(smem_v)) = 0` here.) The ~67 KiB of headroom is precisely enough to double-buffer Q (+32 KiB) — FA3 has the room but deliberately does not (see Q2).

## 4. Same source kernel; paged-vs-dense is a COMPILE-TIME template bool, and paged itself splits into TWO specializations

There is no runtime flag inside one kernel. `PagedKVNonTMA` is a template parameter threaded through `run_flash_fwd<..., bool PagedKVNonTMA, ...>` (`flash_fwd_launch_template.h:29`) and dispatched via a compile-time switch in `flash_api.cpp:274`:
```cpp
PAGEDKV_SWITCH(params.page_table && !params.pagedkv_tma, PagedKVNonTMA, [&] { ...
    run_mha_fwd_<Arch, cutlass::bfloat16_t, 128, 128, Split, PagedKVNonTMA, Has_softcap, PackGQA>(params, stream);
```

So FA3 compiles **three distinct kernels** for the paged decision space, chosen by `get_pagedkv_tma()` (`flash_api.cpp:434-444`):
1. **Dense** — `page_table==nullptr`, TMA KV.
2. **Paged + TMA** (`pagedkv_tma=true` ⇒ `PagedKVNonTMA=false`): the *same TMA kernel* as dense, but the TMA descriptor is driven by a page table (`paged_kv_manager.load_page_table_TMA`, `:842`). Requires `page_size % kBlockN == 0` and enough Q rows (`:443`).
3. **Paged + non-TMA** (`page_table && !pagedkv_tma` ⇒ `PagedKVNonTMA=true`): `Use_TMA_KV=false` (`:59`), K/V loaded by **cp.async gather** (`load_page_table` + `PipelineAsync` instead of `PipelineTmaAsync`, `flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h:295-297`), and it force-enables `PackGQA` (`flash_api.cpp:449`).

Because `PagedKVNonTMA` is a compile-time constant, it also swaps the *tile size* (`tile_size.h:44`: the `paged_kv_non_TMA` arg only bumps kBlockN in the non-causal case), the pipeline class, register split (`LoadRegisterRequirement`, `flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h:86`), and PackGQA — none of which cost anything in the branches not taken. The persistent scheduler is shared across all of them (`UsePersistentScheduler = Arch>=90 ? !(Split && !Varlen)`, `flash_fwd_launch_template.h:77`; causal→`DynamicPersistentTileScheduler`, `:67-69`).

**Takeaway for your case:** FA3 does *not* run one kernel with runtime dense/paged flags — it specializes at compile time (`PagedKVNonTMA` template bool), and further splits paged into a TMA variant (reusing the dense TMA kernel) and a cp.async variant. Your single dense-TMA + paged-COOP persistent kernel is exactly the compromise FA3 avoids by templating.
